I farm 19.1 mu in a wheat-maize rotation, and I am 64 with a one-person household, so I will keep the plan practical, familiar, and not too labor-intensive. I have 45 years of experience, so I do not want to take risks with seed or management that could fail in a bad year. Because I have well irrigation, I will rely on stable water supply to protect yield, but I still want to control input costs. For wheat, I will use improved seed, keep fertilizer at a medium level, irrigate at the key stages, and use rotary tillage because it is easier for me to manage than deep ploughing every year. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because maize responds well to it and the yield is more reliable. I will fertilize maize a bit more heavily on nitrogen than wheat, irrigate in the main water-demand periods, and keep pesticide sprays limited to what is needed. My main goal is stable production from both crops with work intensity and cost that I can still handle myself.
